_comment: Single source of radio profiles: band of interest, channel markers and meshing rules. Read by the solver app (preview screen) and the plugin; users adjust and save copies, and can reset to these. Frequencies in Hz. Each profile carries a source and a status: verified = read from a source on the date given, unverified = from general knowledge or a source that could not be retrieved (a one-line edit here fixes a wrong number; no code holds these values). Three nested ranges per profile: the band of interest (what the user cares about, shaded on the S11 plot), the reported sweep (band widened by sweep_margin_fraction of the frequency so a resonance that is 15 percent off is still visible), and the excitation band (sweep widened by excitation_margin_fraction of its width so the source spectrum has no deep edge where S11 = 2V/Vs - 1 would be noisy).

meshing.source: assumed: cells per wavelength in the dielectric at the highest swept frequency; 20 is the usual FDTD rule of thumb, to be confirmed by convergence tests (docs/PLAN.md next steps). Fine cells near small features are derived from the geometry, not stored here.

2g4.name: Wi-Fi 2.4 GHz (802.11b/g/n/ax)
2g4.source: 2400-2483.5 MHz ISM band; channels 1, 6, 11 non-overlapping, 22 MHz wide (Wikipedia '2.4 GHz radio use', electronics-notes pages), status: verified 2026-11-19

5g.name: Wi-Fi 5 GHz (U-NII-1 to U-NII-3)
5g.source: U-NII-1 5150-5250 MHz and U-NII-3 5725-5850 MHz (radio-electronics.com U-NII page, FCC material); the full 5 GHz allocation has gaps (DFS bands) and U-NII-4 5850-5925 is largely not available to Wi-Fi; status: verified 2026-11-19 from secondary sources, check 47 CFR Part 15 Subpart E for the exact edges

6g.name: Wi-Fi 6 GHz (6E, U-NII-5 to U-NII-8, US)
6g.source: FCC order of April 2020: 5925-7125 MHz in U-NII-5 (5925-6425), U-NII-6 (6425-6525), U-NII-7 (6525-6875), U-NII-8 (6875-7125); other regions differ (fcc.gov, Federal Register 2025-02962); status: verified 2026-11-19

le.name: Bluetooth Low Energy / Classic (2.4 GHz)
le.source: LE channel centres 2402-2480 MHz, 40 channels of 2 MHz, advertising on 37, 38, 39 (electronics-notes.com, everythingrf.com); the system band is 2400-2483.5 MHz; status: verified 2026-11-19

2g4.name: Zigbee 2.4 GHz (channels 11-26)
2g4.source: 16 channels, 11-26, 2 MHz wide, 5 MHz spacing, ch 11 at 2405 MHz, ch 26 at 2480 MHz (everythingrf.com, rfwireless-world.com, NXP JN-AN-1079); status: verified 2026-11-19

subghz_eu.name: Zigbee/802.15.4 sub-GHz Europe (868 MHz)
subghz_eu.source: IEEE 802.15.4 868-868.6 MHz; from general knowledge, not re-read in this session; status: unverified

subghz_us.name: Zigbee/802.15.4 sub-GHz Americas (915 MHz)
subghz_us.source: IEEE 802.15.4 902-928 MHz; from general knowledge, not re-read in this session; status: unverified

2g4.name: LWMesh 2.4 GHz (802.15.4 radios such as AT86RF231)
2g4.source: LWMesh runs on Atmel/Microchip 802.15.4 transceivers; the release notes list AT86RF231 and AT86RF212 (microchip.com AVR2130/AN42028 search results). AT86RF231 being a 2.4 GHz part and AT86RF212 a sub-GHz part is general knowledge; the developer guide's frequency band section (5.2.4) could not be retrieved, so the 2.4 GHz default is the 802.15.4 2.4 GHz plan; status: unverified

subghz_eu.name: LWMesh sub-GHz Europe (868 MHz, e.g. AT86RF212)
subghz_eu.source: see the 2.4 GHz entry; status: unverified

subghz_us.name: LWMesh sub-GHz Americas (915 MHz, e.g. AT86RF212)
subghz_us.source: see the 2.4 GHz entry; status: unverified

ch5_ch9.name: UWB channels 5 and 9 (6.0 to 8.5 GHz)
ch5_ch9.source: channel 5 centre 6489.6 MHz, channel 9 centre 7987.2 MHz, bandwidth 499.2 MHz (arXiv 2202.02190 overview table, FiRa white paper, LitePoint white paper; other channels' values disagree between sources and are not used); status: verified 2026-11-19. Note: dielectric loss is represented by a conductivity set at the band centre, a coarser approximation over this 2.5 GHz span than at 2.4 GHz

default.name: Custom (starts at 2.4 GHz ISM; set your own band)
default.source: our choice: the most common hobbyist and engineer band and this project's first target
